meta.title: Synthetic credit-limit RCT
meta.framing: Synthetic credit-limit RCT with known segments and true CATE. I built Sleeping Dogs around the contact-saturation idea from Phase 1. Outcome = good_standing at 3 months.

segments.traits: Moderate utilization, decent payment history, more App / Urban. True CATE about +0.15 to +0.20.
High payment consistency, low utilization. True CATE near 0 (basically noise).
Low payment consistency, high utilization. True CATE near 0 (basically noise).
High utilization, lots of active lines, more Rural / CallCenter (too much contact). True CATE about -0.10 to -0.15.

ops_summaries.deploy_line: If you used T-learner and treated its top decile, you would hit 95.5% true Persuadables and 0.1% true Sleeping Dogs.
If you used CausalForestDML and treated its top decile, you would hit 100.0% true Persuadables and 0.0% true Sleeping Dogs.

segment_recovery.safer_line: Lower Sleeping Dogs contamination in top decile: CausalForestDML (0.00%).

metric_tradeoff.note: So CausalForestDML is better on PEHE and keeps Sleeping Dogs out of the top decile. T-learner is better on Qini. If I cared more about not hurting people or getting effect sizes right, I would lean CF. If the goal is just a strong overall ranking curve, T-learner looks fine.
